name: Synthetic Convertible Bond
summary: A corporate bond position plus a long call on the issuer's equity, reproducing a convertible bond's payoff - coupon and principal from the bond, equity upside from the call - without the issuer's embedded conversion terms.

legs.strike_rule: corporate bond sleeve: LQD (investment grade) or an individual issue if accessible; 85-95% of the allocation
the issuer's (or the sector proxy's) equity, call delta 0.30-0.45

max_profit: UNLIMITED above the call strike, plus bond coupons
max_loss: call premium + any credit loss on the bond sleeve; unlike the 90/10 structure the bond leg carries real credit and duration risk
breakevens: call strike + premium per share, net of coupons received over the holding period

greeks.delta: +30 to +45 per call; the bond sleeve adds rate duration, not equity delta
greeks.theta: negative on the call, positive from coupon accrual

when_to_use: When the system wants convertible-like exposure but the actual convertible is illiquid, expensively structured, or unavailable to a retail account - or to express 'this credit is fine and the equity is cheap' as two separable positions that can be managed independently.
entry_rules: Bond sleeve must be a liquid ETF (LQD, VCIT, or HYG for the high-yield version) unless a specific issue is genuinely tradeable in the account; single-issue corporate bonds are not reliably accessible on Alpaca.
Call premium <= the sleeve's expected coupon income over the call's life. Same discipline as the 90/10: spend the carry, not the principal.
Call delta 0.30-0.45, DTE >= 180, IV rank <= 50 at purchase, OI >= 250.
If using a single-name call, the issuer's equity must have no going-concern flag, and the credit and the equity must be the same entity - otherwise this is just a bond plus an unrelated call.
Total equity-option premium at risk <= 4% of equity per year.
Long call only, no short legs.
management_rules: Roll the call at 90 DTE or take profit at 100% gain, funding the next cycle only from accumulated coupons.
Sell the call and hold the bond sleeve alone if the credit deteriorates (ETF price down more than 2 x its 12-month standard deviation) - the equity leg is the first thing to cut.
Rebalance the sleeve to target weight quarterly.
Never lever the bond sleeve to buy more calls.
exit_rules: Close the long call at least 2 trading days before expiration; never auto-exercise into shares.
Sell the call if delta >= 0.90 with extrinsic < $0.20 - it has become a share proxy with exercise risk.
Unwind the whole hybrid if the call's remaining value plus the sleeve's mark falls below the floor the structure was built to protect.
assignment_risk: No short legs, therefore no assignment risk. The only share-delivery path is auto-exercise of a long ITM call, eliminated by the pre-expiry close rule.
buying_power: Cash for the bond sleeve plus the call premium; no margin required.
liquidity_needs: LQD/HYG are liquid; the equity call must have OI >= 250 at the chosen LEAPS strike.
common_mistakes: Treating the bond sleeve as risk-free (it is not - credit and duration both bite); buying the call with principal after coupons fail to cover it; pairing a credit ETF with a call on an unrelated index and calling it a convertible.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
